## R Markdown

Importing Data from Statistical Software and Databases

R allows users to import data from statistical software and databases. It provides various functions and packages for accessing, reading, and working with data from different sources.

```{r install_packages2, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("rmarkdown")
library(rmarkdown)
library(knitr)

```

## 2. Importing data from a Database Management System (DBMS)

A Database Management System (DBMS) organizes and stores structured data in tables. R can connect to a database, run SQL queries to retrieve specific information, and import the results into a data frame for analysis.

Common examples of database management systems include:

*MySQL
* PostgreSQL 
*Microsoft SQL Server
* Oracle Database 
*SQLite

### Importing data from MySQL

```{r import_MYSQL_data}
library(DBI)
library(RMariaDB)

con <- dbConnect(RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
                 host = "localhost",
                 user = "root",
                 password = "")

```

### create a small sample database

```{r create_sample_db}
dbExecute(con, "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS PayrollDB")
dbExecute(con, "USE PayrollDB")

dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS employees")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS departments")
dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS positions")

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE departments (
  DepartmentID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  DepartmentName VARCHAR(50))")

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE positions (
  PositionID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  PositionName VARCHAR(50))")

dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE employees (
  EmployeeID INT PRIMARY KEY,
  DepartmentID INT,
  PositionID INT,
  EmploymentDate DATE,
  Status VARCHAR(20))")

dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO departments VALUES
  (1,'Finance'),(2,'Human Resources'),(3,'IT')")

dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO positions VALUES
  (1,'Accountant'),(2,'HR Officer'),(3,'Developer'),(4,'Manager')")

dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO employees VALUES
  (101,1,1,'2022-03-15','Active'),
  (102,2,2,'2021-07-01','Active'),
  (103,3,3,'2023-01-10','Active'),
  (104,3,4,'2020-05-20','Inactive'),
  (105,1,4,'2019-11-02','Active'),
  (106,2,2,'2024-02-12','Active')")
```

### Check the database was created

```{r}
Sys.setenv(MYSQL_PWD = "")

con <- dbConnect(
  RMariaDB::MariaDB(),
  dbname   = "PayrollDB",
  host     = "127.0.0.1",
  port     = 3306,
  user     = "root",
  password = Sys.getenv("MYSQL_PWD")
)

employees <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, d.DepartmentName, p.PositionName,
         e.EmploymentDate, e.Status
  FROM payrolldb.employees e
  JOIN payrolldb.positions p   ON p.PositionID   = e.PositionID
  JOIN payrolldb.departments d ON d.DepartmentID = e.DepartmentID
")

dbDisconnect(con)
head(employees)
```
